chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from Aban ibn Uthman, from al-Fadl ibn Abd al-Malik, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When a group of people are in a town and they pray four rak'at, if there is among them someone to deliver the sermon to them, they combine (the prayers), if they are five people. And the two rak'at were established because of the two sermons.'

key_terms.جَمَّعُوا: They combined (referring to combining the two rak'at into a four-rak'at structure with two sermons)
key_terms.يَخْطُبُ بِهِمْ: To deliver the sermon to them

ai.seo_question: What is the number of rak'at and sermons for Friday prayer when performed by a small group of five people?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the congregational Friday prayer (Salat al-Jumu'ah) and the noon prayer (Salat al-Zuhr) when performed by a small group. It establishes that the reduction to two rak'at is specifically tied to the presence of two sermons (khatbatayn), implying that without a designated preacher, the prayer reverts to the four-rak'ah format of Zuhr. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that the sermon is an integral component defining the ritual structure of Jumu'ah.
